weather_report:
Midday in Perth arrives under a dappled ceiling of broken cloud, the sun slipping in and out like a restless performer, casting crisp light one minute and a gentle wash the next. The day looks clear enough for long views yet softened at the edges, with a touch of glare whenever the sun breaks free. Expect intermittent sunshine through the afternoon as that patchwork holds; UV is likely strong around these hours even with the cloud cover, so a hat, sunglasses, and a dab of sunscreen will be your quiet companions.

It’s a pleasant, come-and-go kind of day: bright spells for momentum, shade for relief. Light, breathable layers feel right, and a small bottle of water in the bag never hurts. Consider a late lunch on a shaded terrace, a calm wander along the river paths when the light softens, or a quick visit to a gallery or bookshop while the sun is at its most opinionated. If you’ve errands, the cloud will take the edge off a walk; if you’ve time, a book on a balcony as the afternoon drifts toward evening will do nicely.
